subject: Private Link & Egress Policy — technical onboarding and action items
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@bluepoint.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-04-02T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Private Link & Egress Policy — technical onboarding and action items

Alex / Samir / Nina — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the technical deep-dive.

Call summary (high level)
- BluePoint will onboard Redwood to support sensitive PHI workloads behind a private connectivity option (preferred: AWS Interface VPC Endpoint / PrivateLink).
- Key requirements called out: fixed egress behavior, DNS resolution for private endpoints (split-horizon), strict IP allowlist for management plane, and optional mTLS for request auth.
- BluePoint will use embeddings + a lightweight reranker for semantic search; they also plan to use Redwood tool-calling/structured-output for downstream retrieval and enrichment.

Open questions / asks for BluePoint (please reply inline)
1) Confirm network option: are you committing to Interface VPC Endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) or do you need a Transit VPC peering option?
2) Provide the source CIDR blocks (or team that owns them) that need to be allowlisted for management traffic and admin access.
3) Do you require mutual TLS for all API traffic, or only for model invocation that touches PHI?
4) Any logging/audit retention constraints (SOC2/PCI/BAA specific) we should surface now?

Redwood technical notes / proposals
- Private connectivity: we can support Interface VPC Endpoint (our preferred production pattern) or customer-managed VPN/peering. Interface Endpoint gives stable private DNS and no need for NAT for inbound control-plane calls.
- Egress & DNS: For model inference that needs third-party APIs, egress can be controlled through a dedicated egress NAT/forwarding path. We recommend split-horizon DNS so your internal name resolves to the interface endpoint and external queries are not leaked.
- Auth: we support short-lived token-based auth (OIDC + mTLS option). If you require mTLS we will provision server certs and accept client certs or issue short-lived certs via our onboarding proxy (sample flow attached).
- Structured output/tool-calling: share the schema you expect for tool responses. We recommend a guarded JSON schema for tool outputs to simplify downstream reranking.
- Embeddings/reranker: plan: 1) index passages with embeddings, 2) vector search for candidate set, 3) Redwood reranker (light fine-tuning or zero-shot depending on quality) to rescore. We can provide sample reranker baseline config.

Next steps (proposed timeline)
- By EOD 2028-04-04 — BluePoint provides CIDR ranges and the network owner's contact (we'll add their contact to bp_network_contacts.vcf).
- 2028-04-06 — technical deep-dive with our infra engineer Marcus Lin (we'll include routing / cert flow / sample configs).
- 2028-04-13 — pilot canary run inside private link (limited traffic) with fallbacks to hosted endpoint in case of incidents.

Attachments: bluepoint_network_diagram.png (diagram you shared), redwood_private_link_config_examples.md (sample config + cert flow), bp_network_contacts.vcf (placeholder).

Thanks — Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

"Make inference predictable and economical"
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@bluepoint.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@bluepoint.com>, Nina Zhou <nina.zhou@netops.bluepoint.com>
Date: 2028-04-02T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private Link & Egress Policy — technical onboarding and action items

Kim — thanks for the concise summary. A few quick answers and clarifications from Network Ops: 

1) We prefer AWS Interface Endpoint (PrivateLink) for the control plane and inference endpoints. Transit peering is a fallback but increases operational blast radius.
2) CIDR ranges: our application subnets are 10.44.32.0/21 and 10.44.40.0/22; management/ops will come from 10.10.0.0/16. I'll confirm exact IGW egress NAT IPs for the pilot by EOD 4/4.
3) mTLS: we want mTLS for any model call involving PHI. For non-PHI inference token-based auth is acceptable.
4) Logging: we need audit logs kept for 1 year for SOC2; access logs for model invocations stored 90 days by default with an option to export longer-term to our S3.

Network contact (attached vCard) — reach out to Nina if you need firewall openings or to validate split-horizon DNS.

We are available for the 4/6 deep-dive; please include your infra lead. On the canary question — we prefer a staged rollout with the option to fail open to the hosted endpoint for <1 hour in case of throttling. Will Redwood support a time-windowed fallback?

Best,
Alex Mercer
Head of Platform Engineering, BluePoint Health
alex.mercer@bluepoint.com

Subject: Re: Private Link & Egress Policy — technical onboarding and action items

Alex — appreciate the details. A few technical clarifications from our side that should help the deep-dive agenda: 

- Interface Endpoint behavior: Redwood will create a customer-scoped interface endpoint in your account (when using PrivateLink we provide an endpoint service and you create the ENI). That preserves private IP paths and resolves to a private DNS name inside your VPC. We will provide the service name and a CloudFormation snippet (see attached redwood_private_link_config_examples.md).
- Egress: If your inference code needs to call external APIs (e.g., knowledge connectors), route those through a controlled NAT/egress proxy. We can also host outbound connector proxies inside your VPC if you want full control (we've done this with two enterprise customers).
- DNS: split-horizon is important — please confirm whether your internal resolver will override our service hostname. If you prefer, we can provide a private DNS override documented in the snippet.
- mTLS and auth: For PHI flows we recommend mutual TLS + short-lived tokens. Implementation patterns:
  * Option A: Customer presents client certs (you manage rotation).
  * Option B: We run an onboarding cert-issuer in your VPC that mints short-lived client certs bound to OIDC tokens (recommended for lower ops burden).
- Structured output/tool-calling: attach sample schema for a tool call response and a simple mapping to reranker input. Please review and tell us if your enrichment step expects nested arrays or a flat facts list.

I'll include Marcus on the deep-dive to cover routing and our private sidecar deployment pattern. Proposed agenda for 4/6 deep-dive (30–45m):
- Introductions & roles (5m)
- Network/CIDR + DNS mapping (10m)
- Auth flow (mTLS/short-lived certs) + sample configs (10m)
- Structured output schema + reranking pipeline (10m)
- Pilot plan & rollback/fallback strategy (5–10m)

Attachments: redwood_private_link_config_examples.md (contains a CloudFormation snippet and sample nginx mTLS proxy), sample_schema_for_toolcalls.json (inline in attachment).

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@bluepoint.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Nina Zhou <nina.zhou@netops.bluepoint.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-04-02T17:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private Link & Egress Policy — technical onboarding and action items

Ben / Kim — that agenda works. A couple of follow-ups from our security team (copied Nina):
- Can Redwood provide guidance on certificate rotation windows and a sample revocation flow? We prefer a short rotation period (7–14d) for client certs in PHI paths.
- On fallback: the canary fail-open window should be configurable per-route. Can your routing policy support 5–60 minute windowed fallback with alerting on failover?
- Audit logs: we also need to understand what fields you log for each inference call (request id, model, token count, originating VPC ENI, username/service-account).

Also — could you share a short example of the structured-output that triggers a tool call (we want to validate how to materialize the plug-in results into our downstream store)?

Alex
